rows.what the ink shows: The first digit has two rounded right lobes. The blackened second digit retains a sloping top entry, straight right upright, and left-projecting baseline foot of 1; its interior is overwritten.
The interval after faisons and before p is covered by the red-brown repair. Only a short right-edge ink hook survives; no complete letter body is recoverable.
A tall initial stem with a lower return and a right loop remain, but several heavy horizontal cancellations merge the intervening bodies and obscure the terminal letter.
A tall left stroke and a short right arch survive on opposite sides of the repair; the central letters are hidden by its opaque vertical strip.
The deletion preserves an initial small loop, an isolated lower diagonal and a final hook, but thick horizontal and sweeping cancellation strokes conceal both word bodies.
The short opening o is followed by the tall b, a crossed t and a separate i dot; the low connected ending reaches a final upright t despite the sweeping deletion crossing its middle.
Between the terminal stroke of limite and the rho expression, the repair covers the writing surface; no distinguishable letter sequence remains.

Rho has an upper-right loop and descending stem, followed by a separately dotted lower i. Inside one opening and one closing parenthesis are two distinct baseline bodies: u has a short left upright, low connecting cup and angled right descent; the separate v is an open rounded cup with a raised right hook. The tall stroke to their left is the opening parenthesis.

The opening R loop, paired lower p returns, and tall crossed t in et survive. Dense zigzag cancellation over the following word leaves a few upper stems and a dot but merges its middle and ending bodies.

The compact form has a short detached initial stroke, rounded loop, small separate cup and joined crossed terminal strokes. The small middle cup cannot securely be assigned to the p or t, so the exact abbreviation remains uncertain.

The coefficient has one baseline rho with a long descending left stem and closed upper right loop, followed by a separate lower-right dotted i; no superscript is present. Lambda would lack that closed loop and descent.
The intervening word falls under the central damaged strip. Only a short curved black remnant survives at its right edge before u; no complete letter sequence can be recovered.
After tout a tiny dark upright reaches the extreme right paper edge. Its top and any separate dot are lost at the crop boundary, so the index cannot be confirmed.
The margin word has a large open C, a compact low or group, two tall joined l strokes, and a stretched low aire ending above the underline.
The span between d'un and hermitien is covered by the damaged strip; the adjoining horizontal joins survive, but the intervening letter bodies do not.
After the descending q and terminal stroke of canonique, the next span enters the opaque damage. No continuous letter body survives to establish the connecting word.

Clear blank paper separates the n and detached apostrophe from one large p-shaped descending stem and right arm; no im or or bodies are present, excluding fully written importe. The following raised hook, short upright and dot lack a secure t crossbar or e loop; the final long q descent and low connected tail support quel.

Below inserted introduit, the old word has an opening c hook, compressed on/s strokes, a detached i dot, a tall looped d and a low joined ère tail. The replacement and red line cross the old word's context, not its main bodies.
The relation immediately after the radical is inside the damaged strip. Neither two nor three continuous parallel bars can be counted, even in the enlarged contrast view.
A small cupped black fragment and a short detached right fragment survive within the damaged area. They do not establish one complete baseline u and both enclosing vertical bars.
Two opening norm strokes, one u with two uprights, and a separate crossing x survive along the upper edge of the damage. No raised glyph occurs; the closing norm pair is obscured.
A broad triangular quantifier has two angled arms crossed by a long bar, followed by a separate compact crossed x. Both sit on the same formula line, with no raised glyph.
Between the inserted arrow and « et », the word has a looped initial d, a taller narrow central stroke, and two separated dotted i strokes.
The deleted word above u(E) is covered by a thick horizontal cancellation. Only a left hook and two small humps remain; the internal letter shapes cannot be separated.
The same nested word has a visible left hook and low humps, but its middle is merged into the heavy cancellation; no complete word is legible.
A tall initial loop is followed by several short upright remnants under a curved cancellation. Those remnants could extend beyond de, but they do not separate reliably into letters.

There is one baseline f, with a tall loop and descending stem, and one small lower-right index i. The zigzag cancellation crosses the upper stem; the surviving shape matches the uncancelled f_i at the right of this same formula.
A tall initial stem with a round lower loop survives at the left, and an open curved remnant survives near the right. A dark horizontal cancellation absorbs the intervening letter bodies.

An initial rounded O/n run, small loops, and a final descending p-like stroke survive around the cancellation. The central ascenders and the compressed final strokes remain too merged to establish every word of On a de plus.

The deleted formula has one u with a raised star, then the sum, one indexed ell, one barred indexed f, and a tensor sign. Beyond that tensor sign there is only the cancellation line and blank paper: no terminal e or index i is written.
The last word has a crossed t, a separate i dot, and a low joined r/e ending. That baseline word is longer than a single indexed f; the preceding connected loop and horizontal tail read on.

The final token has a tall slanted stroke, two rightward arms and a lower loop, followed by a low long tail. En is plausible, but the dark join does not cleanly separate the initial letter from the following stroke.
At the same nested token, the slanted initial and lower loop could form E, with a flattened n to the right; the merged join leaves that reading uncertain.
